title: 16-bit Pixel Art Sprite (SDXL)
description: SNES/Genesis-era 16-bit pixel art character sprite. Perfect for indie game dev content, retro gaming YouTube, and itch.io showcase.

prompt.main: 16-bit pixel art character sprite, brave knight with sword and shield, side view, 4 frame walk animation strip, snes rpg style, limited 16 color palette, transparent background, 64x64 pixel grid, teraria inspired --ar 4:3
prompt.negative: hd, modern, 3d, smooth, high resolution, anti-aliased

explained.why: Dreamshaper + high CFG handles pixel art well.
Higher CFG (9) enforces pixel structure. Lower CFG blurs the pixel boundaries.

tutorial.intro: Pixel art = specific resolution + specific color limit + "transparent background" + named system.
steps: Format: 16-bit pixel art character sprite, 64x64 pixel grid, transparent background — resolution + format.
Subject: brave knight with sword and shield, side view, 4 frame walk animation strip — character + animation strip.
Style: snes rpg style, limited 16 color palette — system + color limit.
Reference: teraria inspired — name a 16-bit-style game.
tutorial.tips: High CFG (9) is essential for pixel art. Low CFG smooths the pixels into noise. Pixel art NEEDS hard edges.

crossModel.flux: Flux struggles with pixel art. SDXL or MJ are better.

faq.q: Why does my pixel art look like a small photo?
faq.a: You forgot the resolution. "64x64 pixel grid" + "limited color palette" forces pixel rendering.

faq.q: How to keep the pixel grid clean?
faq.a: High CFG (9) + DPM++ SDE sampler. Anti-aliasing ruins pixel art.
SDXL + Dreamshaper for sprites. Pixel art needs the "limited palette" cue.
